title: On-call Bridge Operator Manual and Customer Status Templates
author: Ayesha Khan
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical operator manual for running an incident bridge (the collaboration channel that coordinates responders), updating public and private status artifacts, and delivering consistent customer communications. It combines a step-by-step bridge playbook, templates for status page and customer notices, thresholds for common SLO-triggered escalations, and guidance for on-call rotations and game day exercises. Use this as the primary runbook for any multi-team restoration effort that spans >15 minutes or affects customer-facing SLOs.

Scope
- Applies to incidents affecting Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, console, and core control plane services (api-gateway-service, inference-router, kv-cache-store, serving-runtime).
- Intended audience: on-call SREs, platform on-call, incident commander (IC), product on-call, customer-success responders.
- Exclusions: single-service tier-4 alerts with a documented ownership playbook (those should follow the service-specific runbook, not this bridge manual).

Quick reference (TL;DR)
1) If an alert crosses SLO thresholds (see SLO thresholds table), create a bridge within 5 minutes.
2) Assign an IC and note the bridge URL in the incident tracker (issue).
3) Use the status templates below for first 15-minute customer notification and hourly updates thereafter.
4) Capture evidence continuously: timelines, traces, guardrail graphs, and command history.
5) Run a postmortem with blameless language within 5 business days.

Roles & responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): leads bridge, determines priority, authorizes customer comms. (Owner: oncall SRE)
- Bridge Operator: creates and manages the bridge, rotates participants, publishes status updates. (Owner: platform on-call)
- Service Owner: leads technical remediation for their service (Owner: owning team)
- Customer Success Liaison: drafts customer-facing notes and triages enterprise customers. (Owner: customer-success)
- Communications Lead: coordinates public status page and support portal messages. (Owner: support)

Incident lifecycle (standardized steps)
1) Detection and initial triage (0–5 minutes)
   - Confirm alert validity: check metric stream, recent deploys, infra events.
   - If >10% 5xx across a region or sustained 3x error-rate over baseline for 5 minutes, escalate to bridge.

2) Bridge creation and staffing (5–10 minutes)
   - Create a Zoom/Google Meet + Slack huddle bridge (use internal bridge template).
   - Add service owners, on-call rotation leads, SRE, and customer-success.
   - Assign IC and Bridge Operator in the first message.

3) Containment & mitigation (10–45 minutes)
   - Capture scope (regions, models, endpoints).
   - If the issue is noisy neighbor/GPUs: throttle bursting and move traffic to fallback pool using routing policy.
   - Apply guarded rollbacks if a deploy is suspected.

4) Recovery & verification (45–120 minutes)
   - Verify volumetrics (traffic, tokens/sec) and error reduction.
   - Promote configuration changes out of staging -> prod only after verification.

5) Customer comms & closure (Ongoing during incident)
   - Send initial customer-facing notice within 15 minutes if customers are impacted.
   - Hourly updates until mitigation, then final incident summary.

6) Post-incident (within 5 business days)
   - IC transitions to Postmortem Owner.
   - Postmortem draft published within 3 business days; final within 5.
   - Workback plan and owners assigned for corrective actions.

SLO thresholds & trigger table
| SLO | Target | Error Budget | Bridge trigger | On-call escalation |
|-----|--------|--------------|----------------|-------------------|
| API availability (regional) | 99.9% monthly | 0.1% | >= 3x baseline 5xxs for 5m or availability < 99.0% | IC + Product on-call |
| Median tail latency (p99) | < 500ms | N/A | p99 > 1500ms for 5m | IC + Serving Runtime |
| Embeddings generation throughput | 98% of committed capacity | N/A | sustained >25% degradation for 10m | IC + GPU-fleet |
\n(Operators: the table above is a plaintext rendition — consult metrics dashboards for exact graphs and query templates.)

Bridge creation checklist (operator-run commands)
1) Create incident issue in tracker (Jira/Issue): title prefixed INC-[service]-YYYYMMDD.
2) Create bridge channel:
   - Slack: /incident create --service api-gateway-service --sev P1 --owner @oncall-sre
   - Conference: create meeting and paste link to Slack bridge.
3) Post starter message (copy/paste the block below into the bridge):

---
BRIDGE STARTED
Incident: [INC-XXXXX]
IC: @<name>
Bridge Operator: @<name>
Services: api-gateway-service, inference-router
Initial impact: brief description
Time stamp: <UTC time>
Next update: within 15 minutes
---

4) Pin critical links: dashboards, traces, deployment history, runbook links.

Status page and customer comm templates
- Use the public status page for broad outages and the private customer portal for enterprise-specific details.
- The Communications Lead must NOT include internal debugging commands or IPs in public notices.

Initial public status template (15-minute notice)
Title: Service degradation affecting Redwood inference endpoints\Body:
We are investigating reports of increased error rates for Redwood inference API in [region]. Customers may experience elevated 5xx errors and longer response times. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will provide an update within 60 minutes.

Private/Enterprise customer notice (first message)\Subject: Incident [INC-XXXXX] — Degraded inference availability in [region]\Body:
Hello [CustomerName],
We are currently investigating increased error rates impacting inference endpoints in [region]. Our team has opened an incident and is actively working on root cause and mitigation. Impact: elevated 5xx responses and degraded latency. Next update: within 60 minutes. For immediate support contact: [CS LIAISON NAME] ([email])

Hourly public update template
Title: Update — Investigation in progress\Body:
We continue to investigate. Current scope: [what changed]. Actions taken: [short bullets]. Next update: in 60 minutes.

Resolution/final summary template
Title: Incident resolved — [INC-XXXXX]\Body:
Summary: Brief summary of root cause and high-level remedial action. Customer impact: who, what, when. Mitigation: what restored service. Follow-up: link to postmortem and planned actions.

Example runbook: High 5xx spike (api-gateway-service)
- Trigger: regional 5xx rate > 3x baseline for 5 min OR >1% request-level errors for 10m.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Bridge up, assign IC and Bridge Operator.
  2) Check recent deploys: gitlab-ci pipeline history and deploy-tag. If a deploy occurred in last 30m, consider rollback.
  3) Examine WAF and edge logs to rule out malformed traffic.
  4) If GPU-side KV errors traced to serving-runtime: scale down inference-router and re-route short TTL traffic to fallback models.
  5) If noisy neighbor suspected: apply per-tenant token limits and shift heavy jobs to reserved pools.

Command examples (internal tooling)
- Create incident: rwi incident create --service api-gateway-service --severity P1 --summary "High 5xx rate"
- Push routing rollback: rwi route set --service inference-router --policy fallback-pool
- Snapshot logs: rwi logs fetch --service api-gateway-service --since 30m --out /tmp/inc-XXXXX-logs.tar.gz

On-call rotation guidance and escalation matrix
- Rotation length: 7 days for primary SRE on-call, with weekend handoff at 09:00 UTC on Monday.
- Shadow week: new on-call should shadow for 1 full rotation before becoming primary.
- Escalation path: Primary -> Secondary (within 10m) -> Engineering manager -> Director of SRE (if >4 hours unresolved and customer-impacting).

Game day design and scoring (playbook owner: SRE learning lead)
- Frequency: quarterly game days; include cross-team participants (SRE, serving runtime, customer-success, product).
- Goals: validate bridge mechanics, public status cadence, and customer comm templates.
- Scenario examples: multi-region traffic routing failure, model-serving kernel miscompilation, noisy neighbor GPU OOM.
- Scoring rubric (pass/fail criteria):
  - Bridge formed and IC assigned within 5m (pass).
  - First customer notice posted within 15m (pass).
  - Recovery procedure executed within scenario run-time window and validated (pass/fail per scenario).

Evidence collection & postmortem requirements
- Evidence: timeline, command log, traces, screenshots of dashboards, SLA impact calc.
- Postmortem template:
  - Summary (1–2 paragraphs)
  - Timeline (minute granularity for first 2 hours, then 5–30m)
  - Root cause analysis (technical and process)
  - Corrective actions (owner and ETA)
  - Preventive measures and follow-up validation plan

Escalation decision ladder (short form)
1) Can the service be restored with a config toggle or routing policy within 15 minutes? If yes, prefer containment-first.
2) Is the incident affecting multiple customers or enterprise SLAs? If yes, escalate to Director after 2 hours.
3) If uncertainty about public impact: default to posting a public status entry labeled \"Investigating\".

Metrics & dashboards to pin in the bridge
- api-gateway-service: requests/sec, 5xx-rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies.
- inference-router: active sessions, token/sec, KV cache hit rate.
- serving-runtime: GPU utilization, OOM rate, model load failures.
- upstream infra: k8s node events, autoscaler activity, network packet drops.

Retention & evidence policy
- Attach all bridge chat logs, meeting recordings (if any), and the incident issue to the postmortem.
- Keep postmortem artifacts centralized for 18 months. High-severity (P0/P1) incidents retained indefinitely in the incident archive.

Appendix A: Bridge message starter (copy-and-paste)
---
BRIDGE STARTED
Incident: [INC-XXXXX]
Severity: P1
IC: @<name>
Bridge Operator: @<name>
Services: [comma-separated list]
Initial impact: [short 1-line summary]
Pinned links:
- Dashboards: <link>
- Traces: <link>
- Deploy history: <link>
- Postmortem template: <link>
First update expected within 15 minutes.
---

Appendix B: Short checklist for Communications Lead
1) Verify impact scope and whether public notice is required.
2) Choose the correct channel (public status page / private enterprise portal).
3) Sanitize any technical details that could reveal customer PII or internal secrets.
4) Approve and publish using the templates above.

Appendix C: Postmortem release checklist
- Draft posted to incident issue (3 business days)
- All evidence attached (5 business days)
- Action items assigned and scheduled in backlog
- Stakeholder review meeting scheduled if customer SLA impacted

Document maintenance
- Owner: SRE-runbook-maintainers (engineering).
- Review cadence: annual or after any P1 incident.
- How to propose edits: open a PR against this page and add reviewers: Marcus Liu, Rita Gomez.
